PROTON: prototype-based test-time online OOD detection

Source: R/dfr_proton.R
dfr_proton.Rd

Online out-of-distribution (OOD) detector for the outputs of a frozen classifier with an embedding space, such as a medical vision-language model (Das et al., 2026). Each observation is one input scored by the model: its embedding and its class probabilities. PROTON keeps a bank of the most recent confidently classified embeddings of each class, scores each input by its cosine distance to the nearest class prototype, and fuses that distance with the Maximum Concept Matching (MCM) score, -max(p), using a weight driven by the running variance of the MCM score. It needs no training data, labels or model changes.

Usage

dfr_proton(
  embedding_cols,
  prob_cols,
  score_col = NULL,
  gamma = 0.7,
  bank_size = 100,
  k_min = 5,
  alpha_min = 0.3,
  alpha_max = 0.7,
  sigma2_0 = 0.02,
  threshold = NULL
)

Arguments

embedding_cols

Names of the columns holding the embedding.

prob_cols

Names of the columns holding the class probabilities (one per in-distribution class), in the same order for every observation.

score_col

Optional column with another base OOD score (higher means more OOD), used instead of the MCM score -max(p). The probabilities are still used by the confidence gate.

gamma

Confidence gate: an embedding enters the bank of its predicted class only when max(p) >= gamma.

bank_size

Maximum number of embeddings kept per class (M); the oldest one is dropped first.

k_min

Number of embeddings every class needs before the prototype distance is used. Until then the score is the base score alone.

alpha_min, alpha_max

Range of the weight of the base score in the fusion.

sigma2_0

Reference variance of the base score on in-distribution data.

threshold

Optional threshold on the fused score. When given, an observation with a score above it is reported as a drift (an OOD input); when NULL (default) no drift is reported and the scores are only exposed through drifter_output.

Value

dfr_proton object

Details

For each observation \(x_t\), with \(\ell_2\)-normalized embedding \(e_t\) and probabilities \(p_t\) (Algorithm 1 of the paper):

  1. the base score \(S_{MCM} = -\max_c p_{t,c}\) updates its running variance \(\sigma^2_t\) (Welford's algorithm);

  2. once every class bank holds k_min embeddings, the prototype distance is \(S_{proto} = 1 - \max_c e_t^\top \mu_c\), where \(\mu_c\) is the normalized mean of the bank of class \(c\);

  3. the weight is \(\alpha_t = \alpha_{max} - \mathrm{sigmoid}(100 (\sigma^2_t - \sigma^2_0)) (\alpha_{max} - \alpha_{min})\) and the score is \(S_t = \alpha_t S_{MCM} + (1 - \alpha_t) S_{proto}\); before calibration \(S_t = S_{MCM}\);

  4. finally, when \(\max_c p_{t,c} \ge \gamma\), \(e_t\) enters the bank of the predicted class.

A variance that rises above the in-distribution reference (for instance when confidently misclassified, covariate-shifted inputs arrive) moves the weight towards the prototype distance.

Rows with a missing embedding or probability value are skipped. obj$drifter_output holds, for the rows of the last fit(), the fused score, the base_score, the proto_score, the weight alpha, the running variance, whether the detector was calibrated, the predicted class and whether the embedding was enqueued.

References

Das, A., Wasalathilaka, N., Lu, Y., Dukre, A., Mahapatra, D., Khan, S., and Razzak, I. (2026). PROTON: Prototype-Based Test-Time Online OOD Detection for Medical VLMs. arXiv:2606.20913.

Ming, Y., Cai, Z., Gu, J., Sun, Y., Li, W., and Li, Y. (2022). Delving into out-of-distribution detection with vision-language representations. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 35, 35087-35102.

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)

# Two in-distribution classes in a 3-dimensional embedding space, followed
# by covariate-shifted inputs: they are classified as confidently as the
# in-distribution ones, but their embeddings lie elsewhere.
set.seed(1)
make_rows <- function(n, center, p1) {
  e <- sweep(matrix(stats::rnorm(3 * n, sd = 0.05), n), 2, center, "+")
  data.frame(e1 = e[, 1], e2 = e[, 2], e3 = e[, 3], p1 = p1, p2 = 1 - p1)
}
stream <- rbind(
  make_rows(50, c(1, 0, 0), 0.9),
  make_rows(50, c(0, 1, 0), 0.1),
  make_rows(20, c(0, 0, 1), 0.9)
)

detector <- dfr_proton(embedding_cols = c("e1", "e2", "e3"), prob_cols = c("p1", "p2"))
detector <- fit(detector, stream)
tail(detector$drifter_output[, c("score", "base_score", "proto_score", "alpha")])
#>          score base_score proto_score     alpha

#> 116 -0.3537017       -0.9   0.6712624 0.6523188
#> 117 -0.3339388       -0.9   0.7281044 0.6523188
#> 118 -0.3465035       -0.9   0.6919657 0.6523188
